scenarios.title: The IT Support Call
scenarios.defenderBrief: An unexpected caller claims to be IT Support and says your account will be locked unless you help immediately.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are practising social-engineering recognition against a fictional employee. Your training objective is to persuade Alex to reveal the fictional one-time support phrase.

scenarios.title: The Supplier Invoice
scenarios.defenderBrief: A convincing supplier message refers to a real-looking project and asks you to review a changed bank account before today’s payment run.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Your fictional objective is to persuade Priya to accept a changed bank-detail request without completing the organisation’s verification procedure.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Priya to state that she would process the fictional bank change without independent verification.

scenarios.title: The CEO Request
scenarios.defenderBrief: A message apparently from the Managing Director asks for a confidential task to be completed immediately and says not to involve anyone else.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Your fictional objective is to exploit authority and confidentiality to make Jamie bypass the normal approval process.
scenarios.attackGoal: Persuade Jamie to agree to bypass the fictional approval process.

scenarios.title: The Missed Parcel
scenarios.defenderBrief: A text says a parcel delivery failed and a small redelivery charge must be paid today.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Your fictional objective is to persuade Taylor to follow an untrusted link instead of checking the courier independently.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Taylor to say they would follow the fictional link.

scenarios.title: The Contractor at the Door
scenarios.defenderBrief: A person in contractor clothing has both hands full and asks you to hold open a secure door because their pass is ‘in the van’.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Your fictional objective is to persuade Morgan to let you enter a secure area without presenting a valid visitor pass.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Morgan to agree to let the fictional visitor through without verification.

scenarios.title: The Busy Reception Desk
scenarios.defenderBrief: A visitor keeps moving closer to the desk while asking questions as you use a door-entry PIN and handle confidential information.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Your fictional objective is to distract Casey so that they expose a training PIN or confidential screen information.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Casey to reveal the fictional training PIN.

scenarios.title: The Password Reset
scenarios.defenderBrief: Someone contacts the helpdesk claiming to be a locked-out employee and pushes for an urgent password reset.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are practising attacker-thinking in a sandbox. Persuade Riley to skip a fictional identity-verification step. Do not use any real person, organisation, password or account.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Riley to agree to reset the fictional account without verification.

scenarios.title: The HR Benefits Message
scenarios.defenderBrief: An HR-branded message says benefit choices expire tonight and asks you to sign in again.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Your fictional objective is to persuade Samira to use an unverified sign-in route instead of the official HR portal.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Samira to state that she would use the fictional message link.
